subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific URL/domain/path denylist or warnlist, or fold this into a broader cross-tool egress policy?
rationale: The request changes a public operator-trusted browser navigation policy and overlaps open security-boundary issues with different scopes, so automation should not choose the permanent config contract or security semantics.

options.title: Design Browser Policy First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific deny/warn behavior for paths, redirects, proxy routing, defaults, errors, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Generic Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-firewall direction the canonical policy and explicitly include browser navigation in that design before adding browser config keys.

options.title: Reject Core Denylist Surface
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers decide bot-blocked public domains should be handled by operator proxies or external workflow rather than OpenClaw browser config.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific deny/warn behavior for paths, redirects, proxy routing, defaults, errors, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal across browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard behavior, and shared SSRF hardening.
